THE CORE IDEA

runs.text: A shortage occurs when quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at the current price. Buyers competing for limited supply put upward pressure on price. A surplus occurs when quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded; sellers then face pressure to lower price. Adjustment tends toward the price where the two quantities are equal.

WORKED EXAMPLE: MEASURING A SHORTAGE

runs.text: The horizontal axis is quantity of gas in thousands of gallons and the vertical axis is price of gas per gallon. D0 slopes downward from price $6 at quantity 0 to quantity 300 thousand at price $0. S0 slopes upward from the origin to price $6 at quantity 300 thousand. The curves intersect at price $3 and quantity 150 thousand. At price $2, quantity demanded is 200 thousand and quantity supplied is 100 thousand. At price $4, quantity demanded is 100 thousand and quantity supplied is 200 thousand.
